pr_body:
Closes #4798

This PR implements a scrollbar for the terminal by turning `ScrollableHandle` into a trait, allowing us to implement a custom scroll handle, `TerminalScrollHandle`. It works by converting terminal lines into pixels that `ScrollableHandle` understands. When `ScrollableHandle` provides a changed offset (e.g., when you drag the scrollbar), we convert this pixel offset back into the number of lines to scroll and update the terminal content accordingly.

While the current version works as expected, I believe the scrollbar's offset updates could potentially be turned into an event. This event could then be subscribed to in `TerminalView`, not needing to update the terminal's offset in the `render` method as it might have performance implications. Further ideas on this are welcome.

Preview:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/560f0aac-4544-4007-8f0b-8833386f608f

Todo:

- [x] Experiment with custom scrollbar responding to terminal mouse scroll  
- [x] Refactor existing scrollbar handle into a trait  
- [x] Update terminal to use the scrollbar trait instead of a custom scrollbar implementation  
- [x] Figure out how scrollbar events like mouse drag should notify the terminal to update its state
- [x] Code clean up
- [x] Scrollbar hide setting for terminal

Release Notes:

- Added scrollbar to terminal

issue_context.title: Missing scrollbar in terminal panel
issue_context.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/zed-industries/community/discussions/1406
Originally posted by **mpassell** April 8, 2023 Even when I have more lines of terminal history than can fit on the screen, no scrollbar appears on the right. Here's an example: ![MissingScrollbar](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/245153/230740919-64cbd8ad-8c0e-461c-8b18-61a276e83778.png) Anyone else? If I drag to select text, I can scroll back that way, so it isn't that the text has been lost.
Zed v0.80.6 (was also present in v0.80.5) MacOS v10.15.7 (let me know if any other environmental info would be helpful)
comments: The terminal is AFAIK based on Alacritty, which does not have scrollbars upstream either. No idea how relevant that is, but here's the upstream PR for adding one: alacritty/alacritty#7231
@JosephTLyons Could this be added to #5393 under design?

I've been trying Zed out tonight and ran into this hard too. Using the built in terminal to do anything with a lot of output is really tedious without a scrollbar. Instead of being able to scrub the output, you have to give your wheel a workout or shift-pageup repeatedly.

A mild shame as it means there is yet another external tool I need to switch between to use Zed. (version control, debugging, and terminal) I get that it isn't really trying to be an IDE, but it feels _so close_ to being able to challenge VSCode. I really like what I see with Zed though. The rest of the OOtB experience on Linux has been pretty great.

As of this [issue report](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/issues/775), it appears [cosmic term](https://github.com/pop-os/cosmic-term) which is based on alacritty does have scrollbar support. Might be helpful maybe.

(Also interesting note, but "add scrollbar" seems to be on alacritty's 0.14 milestone!)
Cosmic term does seem promising (rust, GPL-3 - matches Zed). @JosephTLyons any chance the project would be willing to try it out in place of Alacritty?

I think it would be better to wait for alacritty to add support, as it's in their [0.14 milestone](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/milestone/26) with the earlier linked [pr](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/pull/7231).
I suppose... that PR is almost a year old and it looks like most of the items associated with that milestone are still open, so it could be a long wait.

If you're here, like me, wondering how to scroll the mountain of clang errors you just received:

- Zed configuration (by settings.json) doesn't have this as an option. I looked there. There is a setting for "alternate scroll" but I'm not quite sure what it does.
- Zed uses Alacritty for the terminal. 
- Alacritty is a terminal emulator library made for OpenGL.
- It doesn't have scrolling but seems to have been considered in the past by Alacritty's developers.

Fortunately, on my laptop I can use [Shift+Page Up] and [Shift+Page Down] shortcuts to navigate the terminal quickly using the keyboard.

**Edit:**
The closest thing I can find to a possible solution is here: [jwilm blog](https://jwilm.io/blog/alacritty-lands-scrollback/)
